headline: Rashi Peripherals to acquire strategic stake in VDA Infosolutions
sum: Rashi Peripherals, India's leading ICT distributor, to acquire a strategic stake in VDA Infosolutions valued at ₹8.5 bn enterprise value and ₹5.5 bn equity valuation, expanding into enterprise technology and digital infrastructure sectors.
implication: The acquisition signals a major ICT distributor's pivot from pure hardware/software distribution into value-added services and managed infrastructure — a structural shift in the Indian tech services ecosystem requiring careful tax structuring (ESOP/carry pools if applicable) and competition law scrutiny under FDI/domestic M&A frameworks.
detail: Rashi Peripherals announced the acquisition of a strategic stake in VDA Infosolutions on 23 June 2026. VDA Infosolutions operates in the fast-growing enterprise technology and digital infrastructure segments. The target enterprise is valued at ₹8.5 billion, with Rashi's equity stake valued at ₹5.5 billion. The move represents Rashi's expansion from its core ICT distribution business into managed services and cloud/infrastructure domains. As a listed acquirer (NSE-listed), the deal triggers continuous disclosure and regulatory reporting obligations.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 – Schedule III (Material Related Party Transactions & M&A Thresholds)
framework.note: central; triggers disclosure if transaction size exceeds 10% of net worth or 5% of turnover — listing entity must file with exchange

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013 – Section 192 (Approval for Related Party Transactions)
framework.note: central; if VDA Infosolutions is a related party (group/promoter-linked), shareholder approval required; if non-related, standard board approval

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 – Regulation 3
framework.note: central if stake crosses 25% threshold; mandatory open offer may be triggered

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 – Schedule 1 (Liberalised Remittance Scheme) / FDI Rules
framework.note: applicable if VDA Infosolutions has foreign investor participation or if Rashi is routing capital through offshore entities

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961 – Section 192-B (Angel Tax) / Section 56(2)(vii) (Deemed Income)
framework.note: amended 2024; flag if VDA Infosolutions is unlisted and founders/employees hold founder shares — excess consideration may trigger deemed income

framework.ref: Competition Act, 2023 – Section 6 (Combinations Requiring CCI Approval)
framework.note: central; if combined turnover of Rashi + VDA exceeds ₹2,000 cr, CCI approval mandatory before completion

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 – Section 7 (Insolvency Resolution)
framework.note: due diligence requirement; must verify VDA Infosolutions has no undisclosed liabilities / ongoing NCLT proceedings

framework.ref: Data Protection Act, 2023 – Section 6 (Data Transfer in M&A)
framework.note: if VDA holds customer/employee personal data, transfer requires consent or regulatory nod; Rashi must conduct DPIA

structure.consideration: Strategic stake acquisition; enterprise value ₹8.5 bn, equity valuation ₹5.5 bn (stake % not disclosed)
conditions: Regulatory clearance (CCI if turnover threshold breached)
Stock exchange approval/vetting of material transaction
Shareholder approval if related party or if Listing Rules mandate it
Due diligence on VDA's financial/legal standing and compliance
approvals: CCI approval likely required if combined turnover > ₹2,000 cr
Rashi shareholder approval if specified in Articles/LODR
structure.novel: Strategic stake (not full acquisition) in a high-growth infrastructure/managed services firm; signals consolidation of IT distribution + services convergence in India's enterprise tech market.

triggers.note: material acquisition by listed entity; continuous disclosure and prior intimation to exchange mandatory
CCI Combination filing required if Rashi + VDA turnover > ₹2,000 cr or assets > ₹600 cr; this deal likely triggers scrutiny in IT services/distribution sector
if stake ≥25%, mandatory open offer triggered; structuring as strategic minority stake (likely <25%) avoids open offer obligation
